facts.statement: The species Morenosaurus stocki was named by Samuel Welles in 1943 to honor Dr. Chester Stock.
facts.quote: The type species is Morenosaurus stocki, first named by Samuel Welles in 1943, in honor of Dr. Chester Stock.

facts.statement: Robert Wallace and Arthur Drescher discovered the species in the Panoche Hills region of Fresno County.
facts.quote: The species was found by Robert Wallace and Arthur Drescher in the Panoche Hills region of Fresno County.

facts.statement: Morenosaurus was an extinct plesiosaur that lived during the Cretaceous period in what is now California.
facts.quote: Morenosaurus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur from the Cretaceous of what is now California.

facts.statement: Morenosaurus is classified in the family Elasmosauridae, though this classification is uncertain.
Studies in the early 2000s suggested that the Morenosaurus fossils were too fragmentary to definitively identify the animal to the family level.
facts.quote: Morenosaurus may have been similar to Elasmosaurus or Thalassomedon, but studies in the early 2000s indicated that the fossils were too scrappy to identify to the family level.

facts.statement: Morenosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The preserved portion of the Morenosaurus skeleton, excluding the head and parts of the neck and paddles, measures 3.63 meters in length.
rejected.quote: the preserved portion of the trunk and tail is 3.63 m long.
